newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares traded mixed as investors relax.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares traded mixed as investors relax.

text.p: Leading Russian shares were mixed on Monday as investors decided to take a breather after a recent sharp rise, traders said.
The Russian Trading System index of 24 shares eased 0.7 percent to 329.48 on total market volume of $21.51 million.
"The day is very slack," said Alexander Fonarkov, a Regent European Securities trader. "If the West is doing anything, it is selling a bit to take profit and reshuffle portfolios."
President Boris Yeltsin's appearance on television on Monday during his meeting with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin failed to encourage the market much.
"There was an attempt at a correction, but Yeltsin's appearance on television on Monday during his meeting with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin failed to encourage the market much.
"There was an attempt at a correction, but Yeltsin's appearance did not let it go far," said Andrei Ippolitov, corporate securities director at IK Prospekt.
News oil company Surgutneftegaz plans to raise its authorised capital to 6.16 trillion roubles from 6.00 trillion roubles, pushed the share price down, Fonarkov said.
"Surgut slipped, but people are still digesting the news," he said, adding the full reaction may be seen in a few days.

Surgutneftegaz ordinaries ended at $0.745 after $0.753 on Friday. Surgut preferred eased to $0.544 from $0.550. LUKoil, which said its total proven Russian reserves were 10.7 billion barrels, making it the world's biggest oil company in terms of reserves, fell to $15.25 from $15.60.
Ippolitov said he expected prices to start rising again at the end of the week, but Fonarkov forecast quiet trading for a couple of weeks.
Moscow phone company MGTS, which named CS First Boston and Salomon Bros as lead managers of its forthcoming Eurobond, rose to $1.40 from $1.30.

Gazprom rose to $0.530 from $0.512 after Regent Fund Management dropped a plan to set up a fund investing in its domestic shares, in competition with its ADSs which rose to $20.600 from $20.005 in London.
